title: U.S. House · West Virginia's 1st District
area: West Virginia's 1st Congressional District, covering the northern and eastern parts of the state including Huntington and Morgantown.

context.text: Incumbent Carol Miller (R) defeated Larry Jackson in the Republican primary on May 12, 2026 with 72.0% of the vote. Vince George defeated Britta Aguirre in the Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote.

candidates.name: Carol Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 12 Republican primary with 72.0% of the vote

summary.text: Carol Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for West Virginia's 1st District, seeking re-election in 2026. A real estate manager and bison farm owner, she served in the West Virginia House of Delegates before her election to Congress in 2018, and she serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means. Her official biography lists her focus as jobs, economic diversification, trade, rural health care access and the state's energy industries.

background.text: Born in Columbus, Ohio, on November 4, 1950, and graduated from Bexley High School in 1968; she is the daughter of Ohio Congressman Samuel L. Devine.
Earned a B.S. from Columbia College in 1972, in political science and history.
Owns and operates Swann Ridge Bison Farm and manages real estate in Huntington, West Virginia.
Lost a 2004 bid for the West Virginia House of Delegates, then won a seat in 2006 by defeating a Democratic incumbent.

Served in the West Virginia House of Delegates from 2006 to 2018, representing the 15th District and later the 16th District after redistricting; she became the first female Majority Whip in the chamber (2017-2018).

Won the 2018 Republican primary for West Virginia's 3rd District and defeated Democrat Richard Ojeda in the general election; she was re-elected in 2020, and after West Virginia lost a seat in the 2020 census she won the redrawn 1st District in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.

Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, on its Trade and Health subcommittees. Her earlier committee assignments included Oversight and Government Reform and Transportation and Infrastructure (2019-2020).
Her official page lists membership in caucuses including the Congressional Coal Caucus, Congressional Energy Export Caucus, Congressional Appalachian Caucus and Bipartisan Rural Health Caucus.
Married to Matt Miller and a mother of two and grandmother of seven, according to her official biography; she lives in Huntington.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Health and Trade subcommittees, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Vince George
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 12 Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote

summary.text: Vince George is a retired public policy analyst and the Democratic nominee for West Virginia's 1st District. According to his Ballotpedia survey responses, he has worked as a teacher, social worker and state and federal programs' eligibility examiner, and he has run for office before. He won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary and lists Medicare for All or a single-payer public option, raising the federal minimum wage to at least $15 an hour, and ending U.S. involvement in overseas wars as his key messages.

background.text: Describes himself as raised in Dunbar and South Charleston, West Virginia, where he attended public schools with four younger siblings.
Earned a graduate degree from West Virginia University in 1984.
Career experience includes working as a policy analyst, social worker, federal and state programs' eligibility examiner, and teacher (WVEA member); describes himself as a retired AFSCME member.
Describes past roles as a student government office holder, political candidate, campaign consultant and conservation lobbyist.
Won the Democratic nomination in the May 12, 2026 primary, defeating Britta Aguirre 53.0% to 47.0%.
Is described in news coverage as a retired public servant, former teacher and community advocate from South Charleston; he lists two children and three grandchildren in his own materials.

priorities.text: "Making life affordable for working West Virginians is my top priority. I support fully funding SNAP, Social Security, and veterans' benefits, and I oppose harmful funding cuts to safety net programs."
"Medicare For All &/or a single payer public option in which no person is left without health & medical coverage."
"More than doubling the Federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour for all workers, expansion of eligibility & benefits for Social Security participants."

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All or a single-payer public option covering everyone.
positions.quote: Medicare For All &/or a single payer public option in which no person is left without health & medical coverage.

positions.quote: More than doubling the Federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour for all workers.

candidates.name: Belinda Fox-Spencer

summary.text: Belinda Fox-Spencer is the Constitution Party nominee for West Virginia's 1st District. She describes herself as a health care professional and small business owner who is not a career politician. She ran for the same seat in 2022 as an independent and says she is running on upholding the Constitution, opposing abortion, defending the Second Amendment and energy independence.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Peterstown High School, a bachelor's degree from Bluefield State College and a bachelor's degree from Mountain State University.

Says she has 22 years of experience in health care and 32 years in small business; her 2022 campaign website said she is from Monroe County, is a small business owner and worked in health care for 20 years as a diagnostic medical sonographer specializing in women's health.

Filed as an independent candidate on July 15, 2022, after that year's primary, for the redrawn 1st District; she received 10,257 votes (4.5%) in the November 2022 general election won by Carol Miller.

priorities.text: A 2022 campaign website statement listed education as a priority, citing high child poverty rates in West Virginia as a barrier to educational quality.

candidates.researchNotes: Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no 2026 campaign statements found.
